title: Complete proof of (7/2, 1) with explicit remainder 49*n^(4/5) for the fixed BK-type family: the Mishra-Santhanam 3.5n - 7d gate elimination fully reproduced and instantiated

claims.statement: Joint CircuitBreaker theorem under rules.md: the following declaration defines ONE fixed eligible total uniform NP family in the pinned full B2 model at actual input length n. Its full guarantee and its declared projection both hold unconditionally, for all sufficiently large integer lengths with the quantifiers specified by the theorem kinds. Both score source claims assert this ENTIRE declaration, not separate lemmas. Let L(n)=c*n^p*(log2 n)^q*(log2 log2 n)^r with the exact parameters in guarantee.leading. Let R(n) be the sum of the monomials in guarantee.remainder.terms, each coefficient times n^exponent*(log2 n)^log_exponent*(log2 log2 n)^loglog_exponent; an empty sum is zero. There exists N such that C_B2(f_n)>=L(n)-R(n) for every integer n>=N. All remainder coefficients are the exact declared constants. claims: Unscored lemma (image dimension): for every state of the gate elimination in proof.md, the image of the injective parameter map Phi contains an affine subspace of dimension a = m - q; hence, for an affine disperser f for dimension d, the restricted function f composed with Phi is nonconstant whenever a >= d. Proof: proof.md, Proposition 2.1.

Unscored lemma (output forms): while a > d, the output of the current circuit in proof.md is neither a constant, nor a nonconstant affine function of the parameters, nor a literal of an AND-type gate whose two parents are unpaired parameters. Proof: proof.md, Lemma 2.3.

Unscored lemma (deterministic irreducible polynomials of odd prime degree over F_2): for every odd prime k there is a single fixed deterministic algorithm, running in time polynomial in k, that outputs a monic irreducible polynomial of degree exactly k over F_2. Proof: field.md, Proposition 2.4 (Berlekamp factoring, Lemma 1.1; cyclotomic chain, Lemma 1.2; nonresidue, Lemma 2.1; binomial irreducibility, Lemma 2.2; trace element, Lemma 2.3). The script verify.py implements this algorithm (Berlekamp subalgebra kernel, with asserted idempotence of every kernel basis vector and a dimension-equals-factor-count check; cyclotomic chain; nonresidue valuation check; X^k - alpha; trace element; minimal polynomial) and executes it for k in {3, 5, 7, 13, 17, 41}; for each of these primes s = v_k(2^ord_k(2) - 1) = 1, so the cyclotomic chain has length one and its extension loop runs zero steps. The file verify-output.txt is the complete transcript of one execution of verify.py (command: python3 -I verify.py), recording exit code 0 and ALL CHECKS PASSED, including agreement of the Berlekamp factorization with a trial-division oracle on hundreds of pseudo-random squarefree inputs of degrees 2-8.

Unscored lemma (arithmetic of the assembly): with W = 2s + 3q + sum of unpaired weights, the stated Delta W bounds of deletions D1-D4 and of Cases 2-10 in proof.md all hold, each with Delta a in {0, -1, -2} and Delta W <= 14*Delta a; Case 8's bound -7 - 2(deg(x)+k) + k1 (with one extra unit when deg(x) = 2) is checked exhaustively over deg(x) in [2,12], k in [1,12], k1 in [0,k], where the tuple (deg, k, k1) = (2,1,1) is verified to be the unique point not meeting -14, and proof.md routes exactly that bottleneck tuple to Cases 9 and 10 (bounds -28 = 14*(-2) and -14 = 14*(-1)). Consequently, for every B_2 circuit C computing an affine disperser for dimension d, 2|C| + 7n >= 14(n-d), i.e. |C| >= (7/2)n - 7d; and for d = floor(6*n^(4/5))+1 <= 6*n^(4/5)+1 this gives C_B2(f_n) >= (7/2)n - 42*n^(4/5) - 7 >= (7/2)n - 49*n^(4/5) for every n >= 1 where the disperser property holds (all n >= 10^12 by disperser.md Theorem A). These exact integer and Fraction checks are what verify.py part 2 executes, and verify-output.txt is the transcript of one complete run.
